chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, raising it, said, 'Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him)':

He judged regarding a man and a woman who both died together in the plague. They both died upon one bed, and the hand and the leg of the man were found upon the woman. So he made the inheritance to be for the man and said: 'He died after her'.
ai.seo_question: How is simultaneous death inheritance determined in Shia jurisprudence when the exact time of death is unknown?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam Ali (peace be upon him) illustrates the principle of *al-ghalabah* (preponderance of evidence) in determining the order of death when simultaneous demise occurs, a key concept in Shia inheritance jurisprudence. By observing that the man's limbs were on top of the woman, he inferred he survived her, thereby triggering the inheritance flow from her to him. This case is foundational in *al-Kafi* for establishing how physical evidence can resolve ambiguity in *mawarith* (inheritance) distribution.
